packs.title: Animals That Sound Made Up
packs.subject: Weird Animals
packs.description: 20 genuinely strange animal facts, explained without myths or exaggeration.

questions.question: How many hearts does a typical octopus have?
questions.explanation: Octopuses have two hearts serving the gills and one pumping blood through the body.

questions.question: Why can an octopus's blood look blue?
options: Its blood has no oxygen carrier
questions.explanation: Hemocyanin uses copper in oxygen transport, giving the blood a blue appearance.

questions.question: Which animal is a mammal that lays eggs?
questions.explanation: Platypuses are monotremes, a small group of egg-laying mammals.

questions.question: In seahorses, which parent typically carries developing young in a brood pouch?
options: Both in the same shared pouch
questions.explanation: Male seahorses carry embryos in a specialised brood pouch.

questions.question: Why are many flamingos pink?
questions.explanation: Carotenoid pigments from food influence their feather colour.

questions.question: What are a pangolin's protective scales mostly made of?
questions.explanation: Pangolin scales consist of keratin, a protein also found in hair and nails.

questions.question: Which body part do butterflies use to sense some tastes?
questions.explanation: Taste receptors on butterfly feet help detect suitable plants.

questions.question: What is unusual about a starfish or sea star's usual movement?
options: It uses many tiny tube feet
questions.explanation: Sea stars use a water vascular system and tube feet for movement.

questions.question: What feature helps a gecko grip many smooth surfaces?
options: Tiny specialised structures on its toe pads
questions.explanation: Microscopic structures on gecko toes enable strong contact with surfaces.

questions.question: What is a narwhal's famous long tusk actually?
options: A horn made of bone alone
A branch stuck to its head
questions.explanation: A narwhal tusk develops from a specialised tooth.

questions.question: Which bird is famous for running fast but cannot fly?
questions.explanation: Ostriches are large flightless birds capable of rapid running.

questions.question: What helps many chameleons see in different directions at once?
questions.explanation: Many chameleons can move their eyes independently to survey surroundings.

questions.question: What is an axolotl widely known for?
questions.explanation: Axolotls can regenerate limbs and other tissues.

questions.question: What is a tardigrade?
questions.explanation: Tardigrades are microscopic animals also called water bears.

questions.question: Why are coral reefs built partly by animals?
options: Coral polyps secrete calcium carbonate skeletons
questions.explanation: Many reef-building corals make hard skeletons over time.

questions.question: Which mammal is capable of sustained true flight?
questions.explanation: Bats can fly using powered wing strokes; gliding mammals cannot sustain powered flight.

questions.question: How do many cuttlefish rapidly alter their visible colours?
options: They swap entire skins every second
They spray coloured seawater onto themselves
questions.explanation: Chromatophores and other skin structures help change appearance.

questions.question: Which creature is a close relative of the octopus?
questions.explanation: Octopuses and squids are cephalopod molluscs.

questions.question: What do many bees communicate with a waggle dance?
options: Which flower has the loudest sound
Information about a food source's direction and distance
questions.explanation: Honeybee dances can convey spatial information about food.

questions.question: Why is a sloth's fur sometimes greenish?
options: Algae may grow on its fur
It is made entirely of leaves
questions.explanation: Algae living in sloth fur can contribute to a greenish tint.

packs.title: Space Has No Chill: Strange Solar System
packs.subject: Strange Space
packs.description: 20 surprising but grounded space facts, including bizarre rotation and impossible vacations.

questions.question: Which planet's rotation period is longer than its year around the Sun?
questions.explanation: Venus takes about 243 Earth days to rotate once and about 225 days to orbit.

questions.question: On which planet would the Sun appear to rise in the west due to retrograde rotation?
questions.explanation: Venus rotates opposite the direction typical of most planets.

questions.question: Which planet appears to roll on its side because of its extreme axial tilt?
questions.explanation: Uranus has an axial tilt near 90 degrees.

questions.question: Which planet is the largest in our Solar System?
questions.explanation: Jupiter has the largest diameter and mass among the planets.

questions.question: Why can astronauts float inside a spacecraft orbiting Earth?
options: They and the spacecraft are in continuous free fall
questions.explanation: An orbit is a form of continuous free fall.

questions.question: Could you safely stand on the Sun's visible surface like solid ground?
options: Yes, because it is made of rock
No, it is hot plasma without a solid surface
questions.explanation: The Sun is a star composed mainly of extremely hot gas and plasma.

questions.question: Which object is Earth's natural satellite?
questions.explanation: The Moon is Earth's natural satellite.

questions.question: What is an asteroid?
options: A small rocky or metallic Solar System body
questions.explanation: Asteroids are smaller bodies orbiting the Sun, often rocky.

questions.question: How does sunlight reach Earth through the vacuum of space?
options: By sound waves carried through vacuum
Through a rope from the Sun
questions.explanation: Light travels through vacuum as electromagnetic waves.

questions.question: Why do stars appear to twinkle when viewed from Earth?
options: Our atmosphere bends their light unevenly
They repeatedly turn off and on
questions.explanation: Atmospheric turbulence changes the path of starlight.

questions.question: Why might a person weigh less on the Moon than on Earth?
options: The Moon's gravitational pull at its surface is weaker
questions.explanation: Weight depends on local gravity, but mass remains nearly the same.

questions.question: What causes the phases of the Moon?
options: We see differing portions of its sunlit half
The Moon turns its lamp on and off
questions.explanation: Lunar phase depends on Sun-Moon-Earth geometry.

questions.question: Why does a comet often develop a tail near the Sun?
options: It is a rocket with a permanent exhaust
Solar heating releases gas and dust pushed away by sunlight and solar wind
questions.explanation: Heat-driven outgassing creates a coma and tails.

questions.question: Which planet is known for a prominent system of icy rings?
questions.explanation: Saturn's rings contain abundant ice particles.

questions.question: Where is the main asteroid belt located?
questions.explanation: The main belt occupies orbits between Mars and Jupiter.

questions.question: What is a light-year?
options: A distance travelled by light in one year
questions.explanation: A light-year is a unit of distance, not time.

questions.question: Why is Mars often called the Red Planet?
options: Its seas are filled with red paint
Every rock there is hot lava
Iron-rich dust and minerals give it a reddish appearance
questions.explanation: Iron oxide contributes to Mars's colour.

questions.question: How many Sun-like stars are at the centre of our Solar System?
questions.explanation: Our planetary system orbits one star, the Sun.

questions.question: Why is space not completely empty even far from Earth?
options: Sparse particles and radiation can still exist
Space is filled with liquid water everywhere
questions.explanation: Interplanetary and interstellar space contain thin matter and radiation.

questions.question: What would an ordinary unprotected human hear from a distant explosion in the vacuum of space?
options: A louder bang than on Earth
A low rumble travelling faster than light
Only an echo from the Moon
questions.explanation: Sound needs a material medium to carry pressure waves.

packs.title: Impossible Physics: What If...?
packs.subject: Physics What-Ifs
packs.description: 20 absurd imaginary experiments with real scientific reasoning and clearly stated assumptions.

questions.question: If you drop a hammer and a feather together in a perfect vacuum, which hits first from the same height?
questions.explanation: In a vacuum both have the same free-fall acceleration.

questions.question: If Earth suddenly had no atmosphere, could ordinary speech travel through open air?
options: Yes, at exactly the same speed
questions.explanation: Sound pressure waves require a medium.

questions.question: If you place a working magnet near a plastic spoon, what should happen in normal conditions?
options: The spoon is not strongly attracted like iron
It always flies to the magnet
questions.explanation: Most ordinary plastics are not ferromagnetic.

questions.question: A sealed transparent jar contains a plant. Can the plant receive light through the glass?
options: No, all glass blocks visible light
Only if the jar is blue
Yes, if the glass transmits that light
questions.explanation: Ordinary transparent glass lets much visible light through.

questions.question: You place an object in a mirror's reflection. Does the reflected object have real physical mass behind the mirror?
options: Yes, equal to the object's mass
questions.explanation: A mirror image is a virtual image, not a physical duplicate.

questions.question: If a submarine dives deeper, what generally happens to the surrounding water pressure?
options: It changes to air pressure only
questions.explanation: Hydrostatic pressure generally rises with depth.

questions.question: Why does a helium-filled balloon tend to rise in ordinary air?
options: Its total average density is lower than displaced air
The balloon is secretly a rocket
questions.explanation: Buoyancy exceeds the total weight of a light balloon.

questions.question: Could an ordinary flashlight beam be heard as a spoken sentence in vacuum by itself?
options: Yes, if the beam is red
Only if you travel faster than it
questions.explanation: Electromagnetic radiation and sound waves are different phenomena.

questions.question: If you put an ice cube in a glass of pure water, what usually happens first?
questions.explanation: Ice is usually less dense than liquid water.

questions.question: If you break a bar magnet in half, how many separate magnetic poles does each ordinary fragment have?
options: A north and a south pole
questions.explanation: Breaking a conventional magnet produces smaller dipoles.

questions.question: If you push a wheeled cart on a smoother floor with the same force, friction is usually...?
questions.explanation: Less friction typically opposes motion on smoother matched surfaces.

questions.question: What happens to a shadow when an opaque object blocks a beam of light?
options: The object converts light into liquid
A darker region appears behind it
questions.explanation: An object prevents some light from reaching the surface.

questions.question: If you put a hot metal spoon into cooler water, which way does heat naturally flow at first?
options: From the spoon directly into sunlight
From the spoon toward the water
From the cooler water into the hotter spoon only
questions.explanation: Heat transfer occurs from higher to lower temperature.

questions.question: If a rubber band stretches, where is energy stored while it is held stretched?
questions.explanation: Deformation stores recoverable elastic energy.

questions.question: Why can a prism split white light into colours?
options: Different wavelengths refract by different amounts
The prism generates new colours from nothing
questions.explanation: Dispersion separates light wavelengths due to different refractive indices.

questions.question: An astronaut takes off their boots while orbiting. Does their body stop having mass?
questions.explanation: Mass is intrinsic; weightlessness does not remove mass.

questions.question: In a vacuum chamber, an electric bell visibly vibrates. What does a person outside hear through the chamber walls if well isolated acoustically?
options: A sound that travels without matter
Little or no sound from the vibrating bell through vacuum
A louder bell than in air
questions.explanation: Ordinary sound cannot cross vacuum; structure-borne leakage depends on isolation.

questions.question: Would a solar panel generate its usual electrical output in complete darkness with no other illumination?
options: Yes, because it stores infinite sunlight
questions.explanation: Photovoltaic panels need incident light to generate power.

questions.question: If you double the time a constant-speed robot moves while keeping its speed unchanged, its travel distance...?
questions.explanation: Distance equals speed times time.

questions.question: If you use a perfect balance to compare 2 kg of sand and 2 kg of marshmallows, which has greater mass?
questions.explanation: Both samples have a mass of 2 kg.

packs.title: Ridiculous Inventions, Sensible Engineering
packs.subject: Wacky Inventions
packs.description: 20 comically odd inventions that teach practical engineering trade-offs and safety.

questions.question: You invent a hat that catches rainwater. What should you consider first?
options: How to promise it cures disease
Whether collected water is clean and safe
How to make it weigh 50 kg
How to hide its weight from wearers
questions.explanation: Collected rainwater can be contaminated and needs proper treatment before drinking.

questions.question: A robot spoon keeps spilling soup. Which design improvement is most useful?
options: Add a steadier gripping and motion control system
questions.explanation: Controlled movements can reduce spills.

questions.question: Your shoes have tiny fans. Which factor limits how long they can run?
questions.explanation: Powered fans need an energy source.

questions.question: A backpack automatically lights up at night. Which sensor could help?
questions.explanation: A light sensor detects low illumination.

questions.question: A smart umbrella keeps opening in strong wind. What design challenge matters?
options: How many stickers fit on a handle
Wind loads on its frame and hinges
The number of emojis on it
Whether it has a catchy name
questions.explanation: Wind produces forces that can damage an umbrella.

questions.question: You invent a quiet alarm for a deaf user. Which alternative output could help?
options: A strong vibration or flashing visual signal
questions.explanation: Multimodal alerts improve accessibility.

questions.question: A solar-powered toy works only in sunlight. What is a practical way to use it after dark?
questions.explanation: Stored electrical energy can power the toy when illumination is absent.

questions.question: An automatic pencil sharpener jams when a pencil is crooked. What could improve reliability?
options: Guide the pencil into the correct position
questions.explanation: Alignment and protective stops can prevent jams.

questions.question: You invent a floating chair for a swimming pool. What must be tested?
questions.explanation: Water devices need stability and safety checks.

questions.question: A robot planter waters crops every hour even when soil is wet. What should you add?
options: Soil moisture sensing and threshold logic
questions.explanation: Sensors can reduce unnecessary irrigation.

questions.question: An absurd giant straw is 20 metres long. What may make drinking through it difficult?
questions.explanation: A long tube increases resistance and may exceed practical suction limits.

questions.question: A bicycle helmet is designed like a pineapple. What matters more than its appearance?
options: Increasing weight as much as possible
questions.explanation: Helmet safety depends on certified protection and fit.

questions.question: A phone-controlled toaster accidentally heats while unattended. What safety feature is important?
questions.explanation: Fail-safe shutdown reduces fire risk.

questions.question: Your robotic pencil case keeps opening in a bag. Which sensor or mechanism helps?
options: A secure latch with intentional opening control
questions.explanation: A latch prevents accidental opening.

questions.question: An elevator can play music but its emergency button is hidden. What is the highest-priority fix?
options: Make emergency controls accessible and visible
questions.explanation: Safety controls outrank entertainment features.

questions.question: An AI-powered fridge guesses every meal incorrectly. How should the team improve it?
options: Test real needs and correct unreliable assumptions
questions.explanation: Feedback and measurable testing support improvement.

questions.question: A paper bridge collapses under a stack of books. What should you do?
options: Test stronger folds and load paths
Keep using the same shape without change
questions.explanation: Fold geometry can improve strength and load distribution.

questions.question: An umbrella follows its owner using GPS but collides with people. Which capability is missing?
options: Reliable local obstacle detection and avoidance
questions.explanation: GPS alone does not detect nearby moving obstacles.

questions.question: A classroom scoreboard updates slowly on bad Wi-Fi. What design helps?
questions.explanation: Explicit recovery and bounded retry improve reliability.

questions.question: A robot cat has ten blinking lights but no privacy policy. What should a responsible designer prioritise?
options: Explain data collection and protect user information
questions.explanation: Privacy and security are essential even for playful devices.
